19 Water flows from a lake into a turbine that is a vertical distance of 90 m below the lake, as shown.
lake
90 m
turbine
The mass flow rate of the water is 2400 kg min–1. The turbine has an efficiency of 75%.
What is the output power of the turbine?
A
26 kW
B
35 kW
C
1.6 MW
D
2.1 MW

hints: Notice the flow rate is $2400 \text{ kg min}^{-1}$, so first convert it to mass per second in $\text{kg s}^{-1}$.
The falling water loses gravitational potential energy $mgh$ with $h = 90 \text{ m}$, so input power is $(m/t)gh$.
Only $75\%$ becomes useful output, so multiply the input power by $0.75$ and check kW against MW.
walkthrough: Convert the mass flow rate to SI units: $(m/t) = 2400/60 = 40 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$.
Input power equals gravitational potential energy lost per second: $P_{in} = (m/t)gh$.
Apply turbine efficiency: $P_{out} = 0.75 \times P_{in} \approx 0.75 \times 35.3 \text{ kW} \approx 26 \text{ kW}$.

A.explanation: Output is $0.75$ times the input $mgh/t$ rate, about $26 \times 10^3 \text{ W}$.

B.explanation: This is the input power from falling water before the $75\%$ efficiency is applied.

C.explanation: This uses $2400 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ instead of $2400 \text{ kg min}^{-1}$, so it is $60$ times too large.

D.explanation: This forgets both the per-minute to per-second conversion and the $75\%$ efficiency.
